paragraphs.title: God as the Caring and Guiding Shepherd

easy.explanation: The verse begins, “The LORD is my shepherd.”
easy.q: How is the LORD described in verse 1?

easy.explanation: The LORD “leadeth me beside the still waters.”
easy.q: Where does the LORD lead the person?

easy.explanation: The psalm says, “He restoreth my soul.”
easy.q: What does the LORD do for the person’s soul?

medium.explanation: Green pastures suggest rest, nourishment, and peaceful provision.
medium.q: What are “green pastures” in the context of the psalm?

answers: Provision, rest, and guidance in right paths
medium.explanation: The LORD provides, gives rest, restores the soul, and leads in paths of righteousness.
medium.q: What sequence is described in verses 1–3?

answers: To receive payment from the person
Because the person is already perfect
medium.explanation: The verse says that He leads “for his name’s sake,” not as a reward for human perfection.
medium.q: Why does the LORD lead the person in the paths of righteousness?

answers: He cares for the person and directs his way
challenge.explanation: The shepherd provides rest and nourishment while also leading along right paths.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from describing the LORD as both a shepherd and a guide?

answers: The person receives provision, satisfaction, and rest
The person is always in danger
challenge.explanation: Together, these phrases describe the LORD’s complete care and provision.
challenge.q: What idea connects “I shall not want” with “the still waters”?

answers: The guidance depends on human achievements
The guidance is given for the LORD’s name
The guidance is meant to punish the person
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the LORD acts for the sake of His own name.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the phrase “for his name’s sake”?

paragraphs.title: Security in the Valley of Danger

answers: Through the valley of the shadow of death
In the house of the LORD
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death.”
easy.q: Where does the person walk in verse 4?

easy.explanation: The psalm says, “I will fear no evil.”
easy.q: What does the person say he will not fear?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.”
easy.q: What brings comfort to the person?

answers: A dangerous place associated with death
A place of celebration and abundance
medium.explanation: The phrase describes a threatening path marked by danger and the fear of death.
medium.q: What does “the valley of the shadow of death” suggest?

answers: Because there is no danger at all
Because the LORD is with him
Because he cannot see the way
medium.explanation: The reason is stated directly: “for thou art with me.”
medium.q: Why does the person fear no evil?

medium.explanation: The shepherd’s rod and staff represent guidance, protection, support, and comfort.
medium.q: What is the role of the rod and the staff in the psalm?

answers: The LORD’s presence and the security He gives
challenge.explanation: Even in danger, the LORD’s presence and His rod and staff provide confidence.
challenge.q: What enables the person to pass through a dangerous way without fear?

answers: The shepherd remains beside the person to protect and guide him
The shepherd abandons the person in the valley
The shepherd leads the person toward his enemies
challenge.explanation: The shepherd’s presence explains why the person can remain secure in a threatening place.
challenge.q: How does “for thou art with me” relate to the shepherd image?

answers: Danger on the way versus security in the LORD’s presence
challenge.explanation: The verse contrasts a deadly valley with the confidence that comes from the LORD being present.
challenge.q: What is the central contrast in verse 4?

easy.explanation: The psalm says, “Thou preparest a table before me.”
easy.q: What does the LORD prepare before the person?

easy.explanation: The table is prepared “in the presence of mine enemies.”
easy.q: In whose presence is the table prepared?

easy.explanation: The phrase “my cup runneth over” expresses fullness and generous provision.
easy.q: What does the overflowing cup express?

answers: The cup is hidden from view
medium.explanation: The phrase describes abundant blessing and satisfaction.
medium.q: What does “my cup runneth over” mean in context?

answers: The person can enjoy provision peacefully despite the threat
The person must flee from the table
The person is left without food
medium.explanation: The table represents protection and abundance even while enemies are nearby.
medium.q: What does the table prepared before the enemies signify?

medium.explanation: The verse says, “Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life.”
medium.q: What follows the person all the days of his life?

answers: In both cases, the person has security despite danger
In both cases, the person receives no help
challenge.explanation: Both passages show the LORD giving security and provision in the presence of threats.
challenge.q: What connection is there between the table before the enemies and the confidence in verse 4?

answers: Present provision leads to lasting fellowship with the LORD
The person leaves the LORD after the meal
challenge.explanation: The psalm moves from present blessing and protection to dwelling with the LORD continually.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the movement from the table and cup to the house of the LORD?

answers: Continual fellowship and lasting security with the LORD
A brief danger in a dark valley
A return to a place of fear
challenge.explanation: The closing statement expresses permanent belonging and fellowship in the LORD’s house.
challenge.q: What does “I will dwell in the house of the LORD for ever” express?
